title: Simulation of a head movement
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $y$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $I$ be a simulated state together with the recorded head and tape information. For Boolean flags $b,f$, define the register bound $B=(8W_N+8)(|y|+1)$, and let $R$ be a register file in which every register is at most $B$, with $1\le R.N1$, $R.Pos\le R.N1$, and $R.N1+1\le B$. In step mode, the program reaches its next phase with register file unchanged; that phase is selected according as moving the input head from position $R.Pos$, with boundary parameter $R.N1-1$ and movement prescribed by $I$ and $b$, yields position $R.Pos2$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
$I$ is a simulated state together with recorded head and tape information
Every register of $R$ is at most $(8W_N+8)(|y|+1)$
caveat: The reachability predicate includes the execution guard requiring the intermediate configurations to satisfy the program's precondition and register bound; its explicit operational definitions are not included in the supplied vocabulary.
